mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last two months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST increased over the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the last month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3 percentage points in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which is a positive indicator for corporate earnings and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% over the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the last month signals a weakening demand, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS decreased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 100,000 in the last month, it signals a recovery in the labor market, which is a positive indicator for economic growth and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS increase > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE was above 6% and PAYEMS increased by more than 100,000 in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points over the last two months signals a robust economic expansion, which is a positive indicator for corporate earnings and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increase and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 2 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO increased and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2 percentage points over the previous two months.
